info.name: Interop Resolution Service
info.description: Every scenario of POST /api/v1/member-ids/resolve and POST /api/v1/member-ids/vendor-map against the dev profile (in-process the member lookup stub on port 9090; start the service with --spring.profiles.active=dev, the default profile is pqa). Run the whole collection with the Collection Runner; each request carries its own tests. /resolve returns the id in one vendor's format when Onyx already knows the vendor; /vendor-map returns the id in every vendor's format when it does not, and Onyx picks the entry for the vendor later. One the member lookup call either way. The member id is sent to the member lookup exactly as the EMR typed it (surrounding whitespace removed); the only check on it is presence. /vendor-map is lenient about what it does not need: only the member id is required; a vendor or any unknown property is accepted and ignored. A sent date is the date judged: an unusable one is a 400, never replaced by today (feedback 20). Every 200 carries a one-sentence "message" right after "outcome". the member lookup's contract has four answers: 200 success, 404 member not found, 400 bad request, 500 internal error. This service maps them one to one: outcome from the records; 200 NOT_FOUND; 400 MEMBER_LOOKUP_REJECTED with the member lookup's text; 503 MEMBER_LOOKUP_UNAVAILABLE. Only an unknown route of this service is a 404 from this service. On NOT_FOUND, "sourceMessage" (type, status, code, text) carries the member lookup's own message when the member lookup sent one.

item.name: 5 the member lookup failures (stub fault ids)
item.description: The member lookup's contract has four answers: 200 success, 404 member not found, 400 bad request, 500 internal error. This service maps them one to one: outcome from the records; 200 NOT_FOUND; 400 MEMBER_LOOKUP_REJECTED with the member lookup's text; 503 MEMBER_LOOKUP_UNAVAILABLE. Only an unknown route of this service is a 404 from this service. Anything else from the the member lookup endpoint (a gateway or proxy answering, not the member lookup) is 503 for 5xx / 429 / 408 and 502 otherwise; a connection failure or read timeout is 503; a 2xx body this service cannot read is 502 MEMBER_LOOKUP_INVALID_RESPONSE. The stub's reserved ids drive these answers: 500500500 (the member lookup 500), 503503503 (read timeout), 400400400 (the member lookup 400), 888888888 (200 with an error-typed message and no members), 202202202 (unreadable body), 887777777 (error message beside a member), 886666666 (record without a member id), 880000000 (only span unreadable). Any id the stub does not know is the member lookup's 404: 200 NOT_FOUND.

request.description: The member lookup's contract: 400 means the member lookup could not process the request as sent. This service forwards it as 400 MEMBER_LOOKUP_REJECTED (details[0].code HTTP_400); the error message is "The member lookup rejected the request" followed by the lookup's own code and text when the member lookup sent a message (the stub sends INVALID_REQUEST). No Retry-After: Onyx must not retry as is. traceId is present because the lookup was made.
